findings.explanation: The firewall rule (source_ranges=["10.8.0.0/28"], network=google_compute_network.cloudrun.name) was designed to restrict ingress to the VPC connector's CIDR range. When the connector was a managed resource it explicitly set network=google_compute_network.cloudrun.name, guaranteeing the firewall applied to the connector's actual network. Now the connector is a data source: the network it is attached to is opaque. If the pre-existing connector is attached to any network other than cloudrun-vpc, the firewall rule is dead infrastructure that provides no protection and misleads operators. The same issue exists in example/examplemulti/module.multi.tf at lines 31 and 38.
findings.remediation: Replace google_compute_network.cloudrun and google_compute_firewall with data source lookups for the network the pre-existing connector is actually attached to, or add an explicit comment that the connector must have been created with network=cloudrun-vpc. The cleanest fix: if the connector is pre-existing infrastructure, so is its network — use data sources for both and remove the resource blocks.
findings.title: VPC network and firewall are orphaned from the data-source connector — ingress restriction is ineffective
